definition: Inert means not moving or reacting; inactive.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word inert. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know inert should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The mill's great waterwheel stood inert through the drought, its buckets dry and its gears silent.
A sluggish pump still turns over, just slowly; inert means it does not turn at all.
An idle engine is simply not being used and would start at a touch; inert goes further — nothing happens even when you try it.
Lifeless goes beyond inert: an inert robot might wake with a patch, but a lifeless one is declared gone for good.

Motionless is purely about not moving and says nothing about response — a heron stalking fish holds perfectly motionless yet is alert to every ripple. Inert makes a double claim: no motion and no response either. The motionless heron strikes the instant a fish appears; something inert answers nothing.

Unresponsive is about failing to react and says nothing about motion — a frozen laptop is unresponsive even while its fan spins and its lights blink. Inert covers both failures at once: an unresponsive machine may still hum with activity, but an inert one shows no motion and no reaction at all.

The festival's parade dragon lies inert in the warehouse eleven months a year — a heap of painted silk and bamboo poles that does not stir when the doors bang or the forklifts rumble past.
Then, each spring, forty drummers and dancers climb inside, and the pile of fabric becomes a creature that ripples down Main Street.

Inert is stronger than idle: an idle machine is merely not in use but could start at the turn of a key, while something inert shows no motion and no response at all — poke it, call it, warm it, and nothing answers.
Inert is the word for total stillness plus total unresponsiveness, and it works best on things — machines, chemicals, bodies under anesthesia.
Its cluster-mate sedentary describes a way of life built around sitting, not an object's dead stillness: a sedentary clerk still types all day, but an inert keyboard answers no keystroke at all.

For eleven years the rover had answered every morning's command with a chirp of telemetry.
Then the dust storm came, and for three weeks the sky over the crater stayed the color of rust.
When the skies finally cleared, mission control sent the wake-up sequence and waited.
Nothing moved on the camera feed, and nothing came back down the antenna.

The flight director kept the listening channel open anyway.
